a: Maintaining and protecting the computer system
tasks.fb: It is systems software, like the OS itself.

tasks.q: Is each program a utility or an application?
tasks.fb: If it looks after the machine, it's a utility.

tasks.q: What does an encryption utility produce?
a: Cyphertext, which is meaningless without the key
tasks.fb: The data is still there, just unreadable.

tasks.q: A laptop with an encrypted drive is stolen. What can the thief read?
a: Everything, once it is plugged in elsewhere
tasks.fb: Which is why organisations encrypt every mobile device.

tasks.q: Defragment this disk: gather each file into one run with the free space at the end.
tasks.fb: Every jump the head avoids is time saved on every future read.
tasks.title: Disk: three files, badly fragmented

tasks.q: Why does defragmentation not help a solid state drive?
a: An SSD has no moving head, so it reaches any block equally quickly, and the extra writes wear it out
tasks.fb: Defragmenting an SSD is at best pointless and at worst harmful.

tasks.q: Why must a program file be compressed losslessly?
a: Losing any data would stop the program working
Programs are too small to compress
tasks.fb: Every byte matters in a program.

tasks.q: A 30 MB photo album is emailed as an 8 MB zip file. What has the utility done?
a: Rewritten the data more efficiently so it can be restored exactly
tasks.fb: Zip is lossless: the photos come back unchanged.

a: A backup of only the files that have changed since the last one
A backup of everything, every time
A backup that deletes the original
tasks.fb: Faster to take, but a restore needs the full backup and every incremental set since.

tasks.q: Why should one backup be kept off-site or offline?
a: A fire, theft or ransomware attack could destroy both copies at once
tasks.fb: A connected backup is not a backup from ransomware's point of view.

tasks.q: Match each problem to the utility that fixes it.
pairs: A hard disk that has become slow to open files
A laptop that is taken off site
Work lost when a drive failed
tasks.fb: Name the utility, what it does, and why it suits the problem.

tasks.q: Which is the best exam answer?
a: Encryption, because it turns the files into cyphertext, so a thief who takes the laptop cannot read them
Encryption, because it makes files smaller

tasks.q: Defragment this disk, then say what the read/write head no longer has to do.
tasks.fb: Files in one run, free space together: fewer jumps, faster reads.

info.title: Utilities used to be separate
info.text: Defragmenters, backup tools and antivirus were once programs you bought. Most are now built into the operating system.

info.title: Keys, not passwords
info.text: An encryption key is far longer than a password. A 256-bit key has more combinations than there are atoms in the observable universe.

info.title: Why disks fragment
info.text: When a file grows and the space after it is taken, the extra has to go elsewhere. Do that for years and files end up in dozens of pieces.

info.title: Zip is everywhere
info.text: A .docx file is really a zip archive: rename one to .zip and open it to find the document's parts inside.

info.title: SSDs do their own thing
info.text: Solid state drives run a process called TRIM instead of defragmentation, marking deleted blocks so they can be reused quickly.
The standard backup advice: three copies, on two types of media, with one off-site. Most data loss stories come from ignoring the last part.

models.title: Inside a hard disk
models.text: The platters spin and the head swings across them. On a fragmented disk it jumps between tracks for a single file.

models.title: Why defragmenting helps
models.text: Tracks are concentric rings. A file written in one run sits on neighbouring tracks, so the head barely moves.
